page: Amazon Web Services m7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory configuration includes 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory rated at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core complex, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector instructions and modern cryptographic acceleration.

The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures. Networking performance provides a baseline throughput of 6 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 3072.58 and Geekbench single-core reaching 1964.0, both placing in the top quartile of evaluated instances. Small-scale language model inference exhibits high throughput, achieving 338.71 tokens per second during text generation on a 135M parameter model. Multithreaded workloads and memory throughput tests generally rank within the median tier, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 14937.0 and large-block uncached read bandwidth of 76.49 GB/s.

From an infrastructure perspective, m7a.4xlarge balances modern DDR5 memory bandwidth and fourth-generation AMD EPYC processing capabilities across moderate density footprints. Because persistent storage requires network-attached volumes, overall I/O performance remains dependent on storage volume configuration. The server is well matched for mid-tier application hosting, continuous integration and build pipelines, enterprise web serving, and memory-balanced database nodes.
